transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thanks for joining the 08:00 change-control huddle. As you know, Welding Cell 5 is running on a controller firmware version that hits end-of-vendor-support this month, and we have a firmware retrofit tentatively scheduled for Friday before the cell's next production run. Before I authorize this work, I need to hear from controls engineering, production planning, and quality on any relevant requirements or concerns. Let's start with controls engineering — what do we need to know about the firmware retrofit?

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical safety requirement. I confirmed with the controller vendor yesterday that a safety bulletin identifies an interlock race condition in the current firmware running on Welding Cell 5. This means the retrofit is not just a support lifecycle issue — it must be completed before the cell's next production run. The work requires exactly 6 hours of energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation. I should also note that the vendor bulletin has not yet been attached to the work order, so we need to get that documented before proceeding.

transcript.text: I need to share my production-capacity check. Alternate Welding Cell 4 can produce exactly 160 of the 240 assemblies by Friday 16:00, but the remaining 80 assemblies must be produced on Cell 5 after the retrofit. One critical constraint: the Cell 4 reservation expires Thursday at noon, and I have not yet entered the temporary reservation in the production system. So we need to lock that in today, and the Cell 5 retrofit must be completed with enough time to run the remaining 80 assemblies before the Friday order is due.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical customer quality requirement. I verified in the customer's quality portal that exactly the first 20 assemblies made after a controller change must be held for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release. This requirement has not yet been copied into our local inspection plan, so we need to account for it before authorizing the retrofit. This means after the Cell 5 firmware retrofit, the first 20 of the 80 assemblies produced on Cell 5 must be quarantined for validation before they can be released to the customer.

Enter the temporary Cell 4 reservation in the production system today to secure 160 assemblies by Friday 16:00, before the Thursday noon reservation expiry.
Schedule the 6-hour energized lockout and post-update safety-I/O validation on Cell 5 with enough time to produce the remaining 80 assemblies before the Friday order is due.

Copy the customer's post-controller-change validation requirement into the local inspection plan, and quarantine the first 20 of 80 Cell 5 assemblies for weld-macro and dimensional validation before release.
